sourceText: B-b264 (merge 2895bbb5e, v0.3.181) fixed a porcelain-parsing bug class in two places: a git() helper that .trim()s the FULL git status --porcelain=v1 output strips the first row leading status space, so the first modified-tracked row path loses its first character (.lattice/x -> lattice/x) and downstream prefix-based classification misfires. Untracked ?? rows are immune, so tests with untracked-only fixtures never catch it. The B-b264 quality reviewer (run B-b264:RR-008) noted other porcelain consumers exist outside that story scope. Open a story to audit every remaining porcelain call site for the same whole-output-trim pattern, fix any that are affected (pattern: read raw via execFileSync without trimming, see gitStatusRows in packages/main/src/handlers/done-prepare.ts and gitRaw in packages/main/src/core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts), and add first-row modified-tracked regression assertions (see assertModifiedTrackedPathExactness in packages/main/src/tasks/done-prepare-merge-rerun-smoke.ts).
normalizedOutcome: Every git status --porcelain consumer in packages/main/src either preserves the first porcelain row byte-exactly through to its parser or is recorded in an audit table as safe (by read pattern, by usage, or immune by format); the four consumers where the corrupted first row reached material/volatile classification (evidence-freshness readMaterialDirtyFiles, cross-host-review assertMaterialCleanForReview, story-query gitPorcelainPaths, partial-done-recovery assertMainWorktreeClean) plus two display-only sites (session brief, story-query DONE-residue text) are fixed with the B-b264 raw-read pattern, and a regression smoke stages a modified-tracked FIRST porcelain row to lock the class out.
acceptanceClaim: node packages/main/dist/tasks/porcelain-first-row-audit-smoke.js passes against the fixed tree (and failed against the pre-fix baseline), asserting for each fixed consumer that a fixture whose first porcelain row is a modified-tracked file classifies with the exact untruncated path.
